::: {#sol-batch-norm-deep}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
batch_grad = first_layer_grad(make_deep(make_norm=nn.BatchNorm1d))
batch_loss, batch_acc = train(make_deep(make_norm=nn.BatchNorm1d))
batch_std = last_block_std(make_deep(make_norm=nn.BatchNorm1d))
print(batch_grad, batch_loss, batch_acc, batch_std)
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# The prose below says batch normalization keeps the last block's output
# from shrinking; stop the render if a change of seed or version breaks that.
assert batch_std > plain_std
```

`r if (py$batch_loss < 0.9 * py$chance_loss) "Yes" else "No"`.
With [batch normalization](#def-batch-norm) in every block,
the training loss after 5 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$batch_loss)`,
and the network classifies `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$batch_acc)`% of the test images correctly.
The [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) at the first layer has size `r sprintf("%.1e", py$batch_grad)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_grad)` without it.
Each block rescales its [pre-activation](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-pre-activation)s to standard deviation 1 before the [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu),
so the values cannot shrink from block to block:
the last block's output has standard deviation `r sprintf("%.3f", py$batch_std)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1e", py$plain_std)` without batch normalization.

:::
